title: End-to-end DR verification harness: SLO-gated restore, circuit-breaker calibration, and progressive load-shedding drills
creator: Ava Ramirez
description: Purpose: Build and validate an automated end-to-end disaster recovery (DR) verification harness that exercises backup integrity, timed restores, SLO-gated promotion criteria, circuit-breaker hysteresis, and staged load-shedding policies. Scope: scheduled tabletop-to-live drills for active-passive regions, an automated restore validation suite that verifies state correctness (KV, tokenstore, snapshots), and tooling to generate progressive load profiles for canary traffic reintroduction. Goals: 1) Ensure a reproducible restore that meets data-consistency assertions within the SLO window; 2) Define SLO gates that determine automatic promotion vs. manual approval; 3) Calibrate circuit-breaker thresholds and load-shedding policies to prevent cascading failures during promotion; 4) Provide dashboards and runbook automation to reduce mean-time-to-recover (MTTR) by 30% compared to current baseline.
acceptance_criteria: Automated restore harness can restore a production snapshot to a warm region and validate key invariants (KV counts, checksums, tokenstore sanity) within a target 30 minute window.
SLO gate service returns explicit pass/fail for restore with documented metrics: p99 latency, successful request ratio, and kv-consistency-score.
Circuit-breaker profiles (soft/hard thresholds, hysteresis) for promotion are codified and unit-tested in the simulation harness.

Progressive load-shedding policy generator produces 3 actionable policies (conservative, balanced, aggressive) that can be applied during promotion and each has documented token-cost and error-rate tradeoffs.
A scheduled drill runbook (tabletop -> live) exists with checklist items, owner assignments, timing, and automatic artifact collection (logs, snapshots, traces).
Post-drill automation generates a postmortem template and metrics snapshot; runbooks updated within 3 business days after drill if gaps were found.
runbook_steps: Pre-drill: Notify stakeholders (SRE, PM, SOC, customer success); reserve dry-run window; snapshot latest production backups and mark immutable.
Pre-checks: Verify snapshot integrity (checksums), catalog completeness, and backup retention policy alignment.
Provision: Spin up restore cluster in passive region using infra-as-code templates pinned to runtime-1.21 image and required secrets via KMS.
Restore: Run automated restore harness that rehydrates tokenstore and KV snapshot; record timing for each phase (metadata, bulk restore, async index rebuilds).
Validate: Execute validation suite (read-after-write tests, delta checksum comparisons, schema assertions, sample end-to-end request flows) and compute kv-consistency-score.
SLO Gate: Evaluate restore results against SLO gate (p99 <= target, error_rate < threshold, kv_consistency_score >= 0.999). If PASS -> proceed to canary, else trigger rollback and tribal-halt.
Circuit-breaker calibration: Run synthetic load generator to test circuit-breaker hysteresis and soft-fail behaviors; tune thresholds to avoid immediate full-cutover and document values.
Canary ramp: Introduce 1% traffic with progressive ramp steps (1% -> 5% -> 15%) using traffic-siphon and observe latency, error budgets, and downstream saturation signals.
Progressive load-shedding: If downstream signals breach thresholds during ramp, apply staged shedding policy from generator (conservative first) and re-evaluate.
Full promotion: Once canary passes 3 consecutive measurement windows, promote passive region to active with controlled drain of original region via traffic-weight adjustments.
Post-promotion: Run end-to-end smoke tests, verify metrics dashboards for 60 minutes, and collect forensic snapshots for auditing.
Rollback: If any critical invariant fails post-promotion, execute rollback plan to revert routing and restore previous active region.
telemetry_and_alerts: Dashboards: Temporary drill dashboard showing restore phase timings, kv_consistency_score, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, and token throughput.
Traces: Ensure sampling is enabled for restore-run and canary requests; attach distributed traces to the drill artifact bucket.
Logs: All restore and canary logs forwarded to retention-bucket with run-id tag for easy retrieval during postmortem.
rollback_plan: Immediate: Flip traffic-weight back to original active region using runbook script (revert-traffic --run-id <id>), disable canary, and enable circuit-breaker hardened mode.
Data: Do not attempt live re-sync; instead spin up snapshot-based restore in the original region if needed.
Communication: Notify stakeholders via incident channel; provide timeline and expected recovery ETA.
Post-action: Preserve artifacts and mark drill as partial failure; schedule hotfix work to address root cause before next drill.
